title: One Node, or Every Node
endLine: Exit sets the stay; entry, fed by blood, sets how many.

scenes.tts: Last time, one node halved its exit rate constant. With entry fixed, it held twice as many cells. But what if every node slowed its exit at once?
scenes.narration: Last time, one node halved its exit rate constant. With entry fixed, it held twice as many cells. But what if every node slowed its exit at once?
scenes.caption: Last time, one node halved its exit rate constant. With entry fixed, it held twice as many cells. But what if every node slowed its exit at once?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and COLOUR MAP without a reset: YELLOW = lymphocytes (the thing that travels and is counted); RED = blood; BLUE = lymph; PURPLE = entry machinery; TEAL = S1P and S1P1, the normal exit; ORANGE = exit slowed or blocked; GREEN = cells held; GREY = organ blocks, axes, labels. THE WORLD, kept all film: the recirculation loop fills the LEFT 62% of the frame and about 70% of its height. A thick RED blood band runs along the top with YELLOW cell dots streaming through it. Below it hang five GREY rounded node blocks in a row, labelled once as 'nodes under the skin' with a small 'schematic: many nodes' tag; each has a RED entry arrow down from the blood band and a TEAL exit arrow into a BLUE lymph line that runs back up to the blood band. At the far left, one GREY 'spleen' block is fed by a RED artery from the band, with its own TEAL exit back to blood. YELLOW dots drift into blocks, wander inside, and leave, continuously. At RIGHT 30%: a tall GREEN stacked bar titled 'where the pool sits', computed from the lesson's rat model (blood, spleen and subcutaneous nodes only): RED segment 'blood 4%' (4.1%), unlabelled GREY spleen segment (32.9%), GREEN segment 'nodes 63%' (63.0%). Recap motion: on 'one node halved', the middle node's TEAL exit turns ORANGE and thins to half; a small GREEN held bar beside that one node doubles in height, tag 'last time: x2'. On 'every node slowed', all five TEAL exit arrows turn ORANGE and thin together; white text across the top: 'Every node at once?' The big stacked bar does not move yet.

Title 'One Node, or Every Node' fades in above the loop for 2 s while the question text fades out. The ORANGE exits return to TEAL (normal) for now. YELLOW dots keep circulating; the stacked bar holds at its starting values.

scenes.tts: Why does the way out set the stay? A lymphocyte in the spleen has no scheduled departure. The fitted model treats leaving as chance. So the same fraction leaves each minute, not the same number. In the rat spleen, it is zero point seven percent a minute. That holds for a thousand cells or a billion.
scenes.narration: Why does the way out set the stay? A lymphocyte in the spleen has no scheduled departure. The fitted model treats leaving as chance. So the same fraction leaves each minute, not the same number. In the rat spleen, it is 0.7 percent a minute. That holds for a thousand cells or a billion.
scenes.caption: Why does the way out set the stay? A lymphocyte in the spleen has no scheduled departure. The fitted model treats leaving as chance. So the same fraction leaves each minute, not the same number. In the rat spleen, it is 0.7 percent a minute. That holds for a thousand cells or a billion.
scenes.visual: Camera eases toward the GREY spleen block until it fills about 65% of the frame height; the rest of the loop stays visible but dimmed at the edges, the stacked bar shrinks to a small inset at top right. Inside the spleen, YELLOW dots wander on random paths; the TEAL exit sits on one wall. On 'no scheduled departure', one dot is tracked with a white ring: it wanders, nears the exit, turns away, wanders again. On 'chance', a minute counter starts ticking at the top. Each tick, a few randomly chosen dots flash and slip out through the TEAL exit; a counter reads '0.7% per minute'. On 'a thousand cells or a billion', the spleen's dot crowd thickens to a dense shimmer (label 'a billion', schematic density) and the ticking continues: each tick still flashes the same visual fraction, and the counter still reads '0.7% per minute'. The crowd then thins back.

scenes.tts: So how fast cells arrive has no effect on how long each stays. Try made-up entry. A thousand naive C D four T cells enter one mouse node each hour. So do a thousand C D eight.
scenes.narration: So how fast cells arrive has no effect on how long each stays. Try made-up entry. A thousand naive CD4 T cells enter one mouse node each hour. So do a thousand CD8.
scenes.caption: So how fast cells arrive has no effect on how long each stays. Try made-up entry. A thousand naive CD4 T cells enter one mouse node each hour. So do a thousand CD8.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back from the spleen and settles on the middle GREY node block, which grows to fill about 60% of the frame height; the rest of the loop dims at the edges. On 'has no effect', a RED entry arrow thickens and thins twice while a TEAL exit dial beside the node stays fixed. On 'CD4', a stream of YELLOW filled dots enters through the RED entry arrow, label 'CD4: 1,000 per h'. On 'CD8', a second stream of YELLOW open rings enters beside it, label 'CD8: 1,000 per h'. The two entry arrows are drawn exactly the same width. A small tag 'made-up entry' sits under them.

scenes.tts: In mice, C D four cells cross a node in about twelve hours. C D eight cells take about twenty-one. So the node holds about one point seven times as many C D eight cells. Entry was equal, so the difference is the stay alone.
scenes.narration: In mice, CD4 cells cross a node in about 12 hours. CD8 cells take about 21. So the node holds about 1.7 times as many CD8 cells. Entry was equal, so the difference is the stay alone.
scenes.caption: In mice, CD4 cells cross a node in about 12 hours. CD8 cells take about 21. So the node holds about 1.7 times as many CD8 cells. Entry was equal, so the difference is the stay alone.
scenes.visual: Inside the same node, filled dots (CD4) and open rings (CD8) wander. Two horizontal stay bars grow from left to right under the node on a shared hours axis, 0 to 24 h: 'CD4 ~12 h' stops at 12.2, 'CD8 ~21 h' stops at 21.2. Then two GREEN held bars rise beside the node, computed as entry x stay with the made-up entry: 'CD4: 12,200' and 'CD8: 21,200'. A bracket between their tops reads 'x1.74'. On 'Entry was equal', the two equal-width entry arrows pulse together. On 'the stay alone', the two stay bars glow while the equal entry arrows dim.

scenes.tts: Here is the whole rule. Exit sets how long each cell stays. Entry sets how many arrive. And entry into a node rises and falls with the cells in blood.
scenes.narration: Here is the whole rule. Exit sets how long each cell stays. Entry sets how many arrive. And entry into a node rises and falls with the cells in blood.
scenes.caption: Here is the whole rule. Exit sets how long each cell stays. Entry sets how many arrive. And entry into a node rises and falls with the cells in blood.
scenes.visual: The CD4 and CD8 bars fade; the camera pulls back to the full loop and the stacked bar returns to full size at right. Two large labels attach to the middle node: on 'Exit sets how long', 'exit: how long' at its TEAL exit arrow, which pulses; on 'Entry sets how many', 'entry: how many' at its RED entry arrow, which pulses. On 'rises and falls with the cells in blood', the YELLOW dots in the RED blood band briefly thin out and every node's RED entry arrow thins with them; then the blood dots return to normal density and the entry arrows widen back. A thin RED link line from the blood band to the 'entry' label reads 'fed by blood'.

scenes.tts: Return to the rat model, kept to blood, spleen and the nodes under the skin. Blood holds about four percent of these cells. Now halve the exit rate constant of all those nodes at once. Each cell stays twice as long. Do the nodes hold twice as many?
scenes.narration: Return to the rat model, kept to blood, spleen and the nodes under the skin. Blood holds about 4 percent of these cells. Now halve the exit rate constant of all those nodes at once. Each cell stays twice as long. Do the nodes hold twice as many?
scenes.caption: Return to the rat model, kept to blood, spleen and the nodes under the skin. Blood holds about 4 percent of these cells. Now halve the exit rate constant of all those nodes at once. Each cell stays twice as long. Do the nodes hold twice as many?
scenes.visual: Full loop and stacked bar. The 'exit' and 'entry' labels fade. Tag at top left: 'rat model: three compartments'. On 'about four percent', the RED 'blood 4%' segment of the stacked bar glows. On 'halve the exit rate constant of all those nodes', all five nodes' TEAL exit arrows turn ORANGE and thin to half width together, label 'all node exits x1/2'. On 'stays twice as long', a small tag 'stay x2' appears beside the node row. White question card at the top: 'Nodes hold twice as many?' The stacked bar has NOT changed yet.

Predict pause. The question card 'Nodes hold twice as many?' stays. YELLOW dots keep drifting through the blood band and nodes; the five ORANGE exits stay thin; the stacked bar holds still at its starting values. No other change.

scenes.tts: No. The pool is closed. Blood's share falls from about four percent to about two and a half. Entry into the nodes falls by the same factor. Their share rises only from about sixty-three percent to seventy-seven. That is one point two three times, not two.
scenes.narration: No. The pool is closed. Blood's share falls from about 4 percent to about 2.5. Entry into the nodes falls by the same factor. Their share rises only from about 63 percent to 77. That is 1.23 times, not 2.
scenes.caption: No. The pool is closed. Blood's share falls from about 4 percent to about 2.5. Entry into the nodes falls by the same factor. Their share rises only from about 63 percent to 77. That is 1.23 times, not 2.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. On 'The pool is closed', a GREY outline closes around the whole loop, tag 'closed pool'. On 'Blood's share falls', the YELLOW dots in the RED blood band visibly thin and the RED segment of the stacked bar shrinks from 4.1% to 2.5% (computed: 1 / (1 + 8.0 + 30.6)), label updating 'blood 2.5%'. On 'Entry into the nodes falls', every node's RED entry arrow thins by the same factor (x0.61). On 'Their share rises', the GREEN nodes segment grows from 63.0% to 77.3%, label 'nodes 77%'; the unlabelled GREY spleen segment shrinks to fit (32.9% to 20.2%, computed). Beside the bar, two tags side by side: 'stay x2' (ORANGE) and 'held x1.23' (GREEN).

scenes.tts: A single draining node is different. It is one among hundreds, so slowing its exit barely changes the blood count. Its entry keeps its old rate. So halving exit doubles what it holds.
scenes.narration: A single draining node is different. It is one among hundreds, so slowing its exit barely changes the blood count. Its entry keeps its old rate. So halving exit doubles what it holds.
scenes.caption: A single draining node is different. It is one among hundreds, so slowing its exit barely changes the blood count. Its entry keeps its old rate. So halving exit doubles what it holds.
scenes.visual: Reset to the starting state: all five exits TEAL again, stacked bar back to 4.1 / 32.9 / 63.0, blood dots at normal density. The node row extends into a faint long line of tiny GREY blocks fading off the edge of the loop, tag 'one among hundreds (schematic)'. Only the middle node's exit turns ORANGE and thins to half; label 'draining node'. On 'barely changes the blood count', the RED blood band and its YELLOW dots stay unchanged, and the stacked bar does not visibly move. On 'keeps its old rate', that node's RED entry arrow pulses at unchanged width. On 'doubles what it holds', a GREEN held bar beside that one node rises to twice its height, tag 'x2'.

scenes.tts: Why hold cells there at all? This node drains a site of immune challenge. The longer stay gives the rare cells that recognise the antigen more time to find it. The shutdown is transient, and exit resumes.
scenes.narration: Why hold cells there at all? This node drains a site of immune challenge. The longer stay gives the rare cells that recognise the antigen more time to find it. The shutdown is transient, and exit resumes.
scenes.caption: Why hold cells there at all? This node drains a site of immune challenge. The longer stay gives the rare cells that recognise the antigen more time to find it. The shutdown is transient, and exit resumes.
scenes.visual: Camera eases into the draining node until it fills about 60% of the frame height. Among many plain YELLOW dots, one YELLOW dot carries a bright white ring, label 'rare matching cell'. A small GREY star-shaped marker sits in the node's centre, label 'antigen'. The ringed dot wanders, misses, wanders again, and on 'more time to find it' reaches the star and both glow. On 'exit resumes', the ORANGE exit arrow widens and turns back to TEAL; tag 'exit resumes'. The GREEN held bar beside the node settles back toward its old height.

scenes.tts: So a node sets the stay, but blood supplies the cells. One node can draw on the whole circulation. When every node draws at once, blood runs short. The gain is then far smaller than the longer stay.
scenes.narration: So a node sets the stay, but blood supplies the cells. One node can draw on the whole circulation. When every node draws at once, blood runs short. The gain is then far smaller than the longer stay.
scenes.caption: So a node sets the stay, but blood supplies the cells. One node can draw on the whole circulation. When every node draws at once, blood runs short. The gain is then far smaller than the longer stay.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full loop and stacked bar. On 'a node sets the stay', the middle node's TEAL exit pulses; on 'blood supplies the cells', the RED blood band and its YELLOW dots pulse. On 'One node can draw', only the middle node's exit thins ORANGE while the blood band stays full and its GREEN held bar rises (x2), then resets. On 'every node draws at once', all five exits thin ORANGE, the blood band's YELLOW dots thin, and the stacked bar replays its shift to 2.5 / 20.2 / 77.3 with the tags 'stay x2' and 'held x1.23' side by side.

End card over the dimmed but still moving loop (YELLOW dots streaming through the RED blood band, into the GREY nodes and out by TEAL exits into BLUE lymph). Large centred white text: 'Exit sets the stay; entry, fed by blood, sets how many.'
